name: Bronchogen

card.summary: An Ala-Glu-Asp-Leu tetrapeptide from Khavinson's lab aimed at lung tissue; rat and cell studies only, no human trials, no appearance link.
card.note: Research peptide; evidence is preclinical and mostly from one research group.

quick.overview:
Bronchogen is a four-amino-acid peptide (Ala-Glu-Asp-Leu) from the Khavinson bioregulator program, described as targeting bronchial and lung tissue.

Published studies are in rats and cell cultures; no human trial was found, and it has no documented appearance use.
quick.mechanism: Reported to stimulate differentiation markers in aged bronchial cell cultures [1] and, in rats with an induced obstructive lung condition, to improve bronchial epithelium and reduce inflammation [2][3]. A biophysical study reported it stabilises DNA against melting [4].
quick.risks: No human safety data; not an approved medicine.

lead: Bronchogen is a synthetic tetrapeptide (Ala-Glu-Asp-Leu, AEDL) developed within Vladimir Khavinson's program on short peptide bioregulators and described as directed at bronchial and lung tissue [4].

Evidence is preclinical. Studies report that it stimulated differentiation markers in aged human bronchial cell cultures [1] and, in rats with obstructive lung pathology, modulated bronchial epithelium and inflammation [2][3]. No human trial is known, and no connection to appearance is documented.

paras: In cultures of human embryonic bronchial cells, expression of the differentiation factors CXCL12 and Hoxa3 declined in late-passage cells and was reported to be stimulated by bronchogen [1]. In rats with obstructive lung pathology, peptide therapy was reported to have anti-inflammatory and regenerative effects and to modulate the morphofunctional state of the bronchial epithelium [2][3]. Related peptides including bronchogen also affected growth of tobacco callus cultures [5]. An AI-generated encyclopedia summary reports a 3.1 degree C rise in DNA melting temperature with bronchogen in biophysical experiments [4].
No studies found. (Search results for "bronchogen" also return unrelated medical reports on bronchogenic cysts, which concern a congenital lung anomaly and not this peptide.)
